Subject: Streaming tail probe & p95/p99 thresholds — Novum next steps

Hi Gideon / Sara,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good alignment on the use case and where latency matters (real-time suggestion surface + streaming transcript enrichment). Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a short live probe scheduled: 

What we heard (summary):
- Primary SLOs: p95 end-to-end <= 200ms, p99 <= 500ms for single-turn streaming responses under your production traffic envelope (bursts to 300 rps, sustained 70 rps).
- Streaming approach: SSE/HTTP chunked streaming from your client through our hosted API, with token-level flushing enabled.
- Fallbacks: you want deterministic failover to batched non-streaming path for larger payloads.

Proposed live probe (what Redwood will run):
1) 2-hour window mimicking your production envelope: 3 traffic profiles (burst, steady, low-latency sampling).
2) Concurrency matrix: 1, 4, 16 concurrent clients producing streaming sessions; each session ~200 tokens avg, variance up to 800.
3) Measure: p50/p95/p99 latency, first-byte, last-byte, and percent of streamed responses that had incremental flushes.
4) Collect traces + kernel-level breakdown (kernel time, queuing, network).

Ask from Novum to enable probe:
- A test endpoint (or allow Redwood to replay TLS-handshake/headers samples) and temporary ingestion key.
- A representative one-hour sample of real request headers/size distribution (we only need metadata, not PII).

I've attached a short probe plan and a small set of anonymized trace examples we can use to bootstrap. Please confirm available windows tomorrow or Friday so we can lock infra and an SRE.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Michael — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The p95/p99 targets you noted are aspirational; our incumbent meets roughly p95 ~230ms and p99 ~620ms today under typical load, but we see big variance during early morning ET bursts.
- We use SSE on the client but terminate TLS at our edge (Fastly). Would Redwood be able to route test traffic through our edge? If not we can spin up a test origin for the probe.
- For concurrency, could we add a 64-concurrency run for the burst profile? We've seen short spikes that high during batch uploads.

Available windows: Friday 2028-03-26 14:00–16:00 ET or Monday 2028-03-29 09:00–11:00 ET. Procurement will also want to join the kickoff if we lock a formal POC.

On the attachments: thank you — we'll take a look and upload a small sanitized request-sample to your shared Drive link.

Regards,
Gideon Park
Senior Platform Ops, Novum Health
